# Does COMP110 Apply Equally to All Majors?

## Summary
This analysis explored whether CS majors and non-CS majors differ in how they experience COMP110. The survey data collected from students earlier this semester was used to compare ratings across three measures: how valuable students find the course, how interesting they find the topics, and whether they would recommend it to others. Students were filtered into two groups — those intending to major in CS and those who are not — and their ratings were compared using bar charts.

## Analysis Findings
The data showed that CS majors consistently rated the course higher across all three measures. CS majors rated the course as valuable at around 5.5 out of 7, while non-CS majors rated it at around 4.9 out of 7. Similarly, CS majors found the topics more interesting, rating it around 5.3 compared to 4.5 for non-CS majors. CS majors were also more likely to recommend the course to others. Since the vast majority of students in COMP110 are non-CS majors, these findings suggest that the course currently applies more to CS majors than to most of the students taking it.

## Conclusion
The data supports the hypothesis that non-CS majors find COMP110 less valuable and interesting than CS majors. Introducing major based group projects where students work on problems relevant to their field of study could make the course more applicable and engaging for the majority of students. While this would require more work from professors and TAs in terms of grading and assignment design, a simplified approach of grouping students into broader interest categories such as natural sciences, social sciences, and business could reduce that burden while still improving the experience for non-CS majors.
